mainTopic: A master's power over his slave's נזירות and vows, and the slave נזיר who ran away
overview: The משנה teaches that a husband can truly cancel (הפרה) his wife's vows, but a master cannot cancel his slave's vows. The master can only force the slave to break his נזירות, and once the slave is freed he must finish it. The גמרא brings a ברייתא that a master can force his slave only regarding נזירות, not other נדרים or ערכין, and asks why, since the פסוק 'לאסר אסר על נפשו' is about all vows. רב ששת (a single cluster of grapes) and then רבא (a single grape seed) try to answer, but each answer is challenged. אביי finally rereads the ברייתא: the master only needs to force the slave for נזירות, because a slave's ordinary vows and oaths never take effect. The source is 'להרע או להיטיב': a person cannot swear to cause harm to others. A second משנה brings a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי about a נזיר slave who ran away. The גמרא rejects the idea that they argue about שמואל's rule and explains that they argue over whether wine or hardship better serves the master.

steps.title: The משנה: a slave's vows are stricter than a wife's
steps.stepSummary: A husband can truly cancel his wife's vows, but a master cannot cancel his slave's vows. A wife's cancelled נזירות is gone forever. A slave who was forced to break his נזירות must finish it once he is freed.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a stricter side to slaves than to women. A husband can cancel his wife's vows, but a master cannot cancel his slave's vows. If a husband cancels his wife's נזירות, it is cancelled forever. If a master 'cancels' his slave's נזירות, then when the slave is freed he must finish his נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares a wife and a slave and shows a way the slave's vow is 'stronger': the master can't really erase it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A husband has a true power of הפרה from the תורה, which wipes out the vow completely. A master has no such power. He can only stop the slave from keeping the vow while the slave is under his control. So the vow is still there, and once the slave is free it comes back into force.

keyTerms.meaning: Went out to freedom; was freed
The state of being a נזיר

steps.confusionAlert: When the משנה says the master 'הפר' for his slave, it does not mean a real cancellation. The master only forced the slave to break the vow for now. That is exactly why the slave must finish it later.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole סוגיא: the master's power is only the power to force, not to cancel. The גמרא next asks when exactly he may use it.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
There is a stringency with slaves more than with women,
for he can cancel his wife's vows,
but he cannot cancel his slave's vows.
If he cancelled for his wife —
it is cancelled forever.
If he 'cancelled' for his slave —
phrases.notes: Here it means he forced the slave to break the נזירות, not a true cancellation.

phrases.english: when the slave goes out to freedom
he completes his נזירות.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband truly cancels his wife's vows forever. A master cannot cancel his slave's vows; a slave forced to break נזירות must complete it after he is freed.

steps.title: ברייתא: a master can force his slave only regarding נזירות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a master may force his slave to break נזירות, but not other נדרים or ערכין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: In what matter can a master force his slave? In נזירות. But not in other vows and not in ערכין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that limits the master's power to force: it works only for נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה told us a master can force his slave to break נזירות. This ברייתא adds that the power stops there. For ordinary נדרים and ערכין, the master cannot force the slave to break his word.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows to give the Temple the fixed 'value' of a person

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Sages taught:
Regarding what can his master force him?
Regarding נזירות,
but not regarding vows and ערכין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the master's power described in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A master may force his slave to break נזירות, but not other נדרים or ערכין.

steps.title: Why is נזירות different? The verse about one's own soul
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes נזירות special and gives the source: 'לאסר אסר על נפשו' means only someone whose soul belongs to himself, which leaves out a slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a נזיר? The תורה says 'to bind a bond on his soul.' This means someone whose soul belongs to him. That leaves out a slave, whose soul does not belong to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ברייתא and gives the פסוק that lets a master force his slave. This is the setup for the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'על נפשו' (on his own soul) teach that the תורה's vow rules apply fully only to a person who owns himself. A slave is owned by his master, so the master can override him. This explains why the master can force him to break נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To bind a bond on his soul' (במדבר 30:3)
Owned by him, belongs to him

phrases.english: What is different about a נזיר?
For the Merciful One said:
"to bind a bond on his soul,"
meaning one whose soul belongs to him —
this leaves out a slave,
whose soul does not belong to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source and reason behind the ברייתא's rule about נזירות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a master may force his slave regarding נזירות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'לאסר אסר על נפשו' excludes a slave, whose soul belongs to his master.

steps.title: Challenge: that verse should apply to all vows
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is the פסוק 'על נפשו', then a master should be able to force his slave regarding all vows too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even with vows too the master should be able to force him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא. The reason just given should cover ordinary vows too, not only נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'לאסר אסר על נפשו' appears in the section about vows in general, not about נזירות in particular. So if it excludes a slave from נזירות, it should exclude him from every vow. Then why did the ברייתא say 'but not regarding vows'?

phrases.english: If so,
then even regarding vows too!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ גַּבֵּי נְדָרִים נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 3 to challenge the ברייתא in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a master cannot force his slave regarding נדרים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source verse speaks of all vows, so its exclusion of a slave should apply to all vows, not only נזירות.

steps.title: רב ששת: the vow was on one cluster of grapes
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the ברייתא is talking about a slave who vowed off one specific cluster of grapes. That vow does not limit him in other things, so the master cannot force him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: What case are we dealing with here? A case where a cluster of grapes was lying in front of the slave and he vowed not to have it. With vows like this, when he is forbidden this cluster he is not forbidden others. So the master cannot force him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge by explaining which kind of vow the ברייתא means. The master really could override vows, but he has no reason to here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow on one cluster does not take anything away from the master, because the slave can still eat other grapes. So the master has no reason to force him to eat this one. A נזיר, by contrast, is forbidden all grape products, which can affect the master, so there the master may force him.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
With what case are we dealing here?
For example, where there was a cluster of grapes
lying in front of him.
Regarding vows,
since when he is forbidden this one
he is not forbidden others —
the master cannot force him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 by limiting the ברייתא to a specific kind of vow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say a master can never force his slave regarding vows, which contradicts the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means a vow on one specific item that doesn't limit the slave generally, so the master has no reason to force him; the פסוק's principle still stands.

steps.title: רב ששת's answer continued: a נזיר is forbidden in everything
steps.stepSummary: This completes רב ששת's answer. With נזירות, being forbidden in one cluster means being forbidden in all grape products, so the master can force him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding נזירות, when he is forbidden in this one cluster, he is forbidden in all of them, so the master can force him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב ששת's answer by giving the other side of the contrast. A נזיר is forbidden in all grape products, so the master may force him to break it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 explained why a vow on one cluster cannot be forced: it limits only that one cluster. נזירות is different because it forbids every grape and grape product, so it really can weaken the slave. That is why the master is allowed to step in.

keyTerms.meaning: He is forbidden in all of them

phrases.english: Regarding נזירות,
where, when he is forbidden in this one, he is forbidden in all of them —
phrases.notes: "This one" is the single cluster of grapes from רב ששת's case in the step before.

phrases.english: he can force him.

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבֵּי נְזִירוּת, דְּכִי מִיתְּסַר בְּהַאי אִיתְּסַר בְּכוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of רב ששת's answer from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case narrowing: a vow on one cluster, compared with נזירות that forbids all grapes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The reason 'על נפשו' should let the master force the slave for any vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only נזירות limits the slave widely enough to weaken him, so only there may the master force him.

steps.title: But with a regular vow he might have only that one cluster
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב ששת. Even a vow on one cluster could weaken the slave if that cluster is the only food he has.
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding vows, can't the case be where there is only this one cluster, so that if he doesn't eat it he becomes weak?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's answer. A one-cluster vow can also weaken the slave if that is all the food there is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's split depended on the idea that a one-cluster vow never weakens the slave. The גמרא points out that the ברייתא says vows cannot be forced with no exceptions, even when the cluster is his only food. So the 'weakening' reason does not fully separate the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Aren't we dealing with (even) a case where...?

phrases.english: But regarding vows,
are we not dealing [even with a case]
where there is only this cluster,
so that if he does not eat it, he becomes weak?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ששת's answer from steps 5 and 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that a vow on one cluster cannot weaken the slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids forcing for all vows, even when the one cluster is his only food and not eating it would weaken him.

steps.title: רבא: the case is a single grape seed
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא means a vow about one grape seed. Losing a seed cannot weaken anyone, so with a regular vow the master cannot force him. A נזיר, though, is also forbidden in other grape products, so there he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: the case is where a grape seed was lying in front of him. With vows, he is forbidden only in this seed, so the master cannot force him. With a נזיר, who is forbidden in other things too, the master can force him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops רב ששת's cluster case and gives a smaller one, a single grape seed. Since a seed hardly feeds anyone, the vow on it can never weaken the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא picks a case where the regular vow clearly causes no weakness, so the question from step 7 seems to go away. נזירות still forbids all grape products, so it still counts as limiting the slave. The basic split between נדרים and נזירות stays the same; only the example changes.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: the previous answer is dropped and a new one is given

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
For example, where a grape seed was lying in front of him.
Regarding vows, it is only in this that he is forbidden —
he cannot force him.
Regarding a נזיר, who is forbidden in other things too —
he can force him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה חַרְצָן מוּנָּח לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב ששת's answer after the challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case to one where the regular vow cannot weaken him at all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A vow on a cluster could be his only food and weaken him.
steps.terutzMaskana: A vow on a single seed never weakens him, so it cannot be forced. נזירות forbids much more, so it can be.

steps.title: But he might have only that one seed
steps.stepSummary: The same challenge returns against רבא. What if the seed is the only food he has, and he would grow weak without it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding vows, can't the case be where there is only this grape seed, so that if he doesn't eat it he becomes weak?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats its earlier challenge in the same words, now aimed at רבא's grape seed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא still says regular vows cannot be forced, even in the extreme case where the seed is his only food. So רבא's answer has the same weakness as רב ששת's. This sets up the need for a completely different approach.

phrases.english: But regarding vows,
are we not dealing [even with a case]
where there is only this grape seed,
so that if he does not eat it, he becomes weak?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגַבֵּי נְדָרִים, מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּלֵיכָּא אֶלָּא הַאי חַרְצָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer with the same question used against רב ששת in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that a vow on a seed cannot weaken the slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the seed is his only food, not eating it would weaken him, yet the ברייתא still says regular vows cannot be forced.

steps.title: אביי: the master only NEEDS to force him for נזירות
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the ברייתא in a new way. It is not saying when the master is allowed to force the slave, but when he needs to. He needs to for נזירות, but not for regular vows or oaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: for what does the master need to force his slave? For נזירות. He does not need to force him for vows, and he does not need to force him for an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי drops the whole 'does it weaken him' approach. He explains that the ברייתא lists the only case where the master has to force the slave in order to stop the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, we read the ברייתא as 'the master MAY force for נזירות but MAY NOT for vows.' אביי reads it as 'the master NEEDS to force only for נזירות.' For regular vows and oaths there is no need to force him; the usual explanation is that those do not take effect on a slave in the first place.
steps.whatToRemember: After two answers based on whether the slave would grow weak are both pushed aside, אביי changes how we read the ברייתא. It means 'needs to force,' not 'may force.' The master must force the slave only for נזירות, not for regular vows or oaths.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read אביי as saying the master is forbidden to force the slave about regular vows. He is saying there is no NEED to force him there.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ends the back-and-forth by changing what the ברייתא is about, instead of searching for yet another case.

phrases.english: Rather, אביי said:
For what does his master need to force him? For נזירות.
phrases.notes: Pay attention to the word "need": אביי is changing the ברייתא from "may force" to "must force."

phrases.english: But he does not need to force him for vows,
and he does not need to force him for an oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְמָה רַבּוֹ צָרִיךְ לִכְפּוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's answer after the challenge in step 9 by reading the ברייתא from step 2 differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ברייתא: 'needs to force' instead of 'may force'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lists when the master is allowed to force his slave, which needed a reason based on weakness.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא lists when the master needs to force the slave. That is only for נזירות; vows and oaths need no forcing.

steps.title: Why is there no need to force the slave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's statement that the master does not need to force the slave in regular vows and oaths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the master does not need to force his slave in vows and oaths. This short question sets up the answer from a פסוק in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, אביי said the master needs to force the slave to break נזירות but not vows or oaths. The גמרא now wants the source. The answer will show that such an oath never takes effect in the first place.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why doesn't the master need to force the slave with vows and oaths, like אביי said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind אביי's new reading in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a master does not need to force his slave when the slave makes a regular vow or oath.

steps.title: A person can only swear about harm that is his own to choose
steps.stepSummary: From 'להרע או להיטיב' we learn that 'doing good' is something in a person's own hands, so 'doing harm' must be too. Harm to others, which is not in a person's hands, is left out. A slave's oath harms his master, so it does not take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the פסוק says, 'to do harm or to do good.' Just as doing good is in his own hands, doing harm must also be in his own hands. This leaves out doing harm to others, which is not in his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from a פסוק about oaths. An oath only works on harm that is his own to choose, and a slave's oath would harm his master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'harm' next to 'good.' Since swearing to do good is up to the person, swearing to do harm must also be limited to what is up to him, like harm to himself. A slave who weakens himself is really harming his master, so his oath has no power, and the master has nothing to force.

keyTerms.meaning: To do harm or to do good (ויקרא 5:4)
Something that is in a person's own hands, his to choose

steps.whatToRemember: An oath only works on things that are in the person's own power. A slave's oath that harms his master never takes effect, so the master does not need to force him. With נזירות, as step 10 said, the master does need to force him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the difference between oaths and נזירות in אביי's reading comes from a פסוק, not from simple logic.

phrases.english: Because the verse says:
"To do harm or to do good,"
just as doing good is in his own hands,
so too, doing harm must be in his own hands.
This leaves out doing harm to others,
which is not in his hands.
phrases.notes: Here the 'others' is the master, who loses out when his slave grows weak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'להרע או להיטיב': an oath works only on harm that is in the person's own hands. A slave's oath harms his master, so it does not take effect, and there is nothing to force.

steps.title: A נזיר slave who ran away from his master
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a slave who took נזירות ran away from his master. רבי מאיר says he may not drink wine. רבי יוסי says he may.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the slave left his master's presence, רבי מאיר says he may not drink wine, and רבי יוסי says he may drink.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a מחלוקת about a slave who accepted נזירות and then ran away from his master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the master could stop the slave from keeping his נזירות. Now the slave has escaped, so the master is no longer there to stop him. רבי מאיר says the נזירות now applies, so no wine. רבי יוסי says he may still drink.

keyTerms.meaning: He left his master's presence, meaning he ran away

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If he passed out of his master's presence,
phrases.notes: This is the slave who took נזירות. He ran away for good but was never set free.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says: he may not drink wine,
and Rabbi Yosei says: he may drink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה that continues the topic of a slave's נזירות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר slave who ran away: רבי מאיר says he may not drink wine; רבי יוסי says he may.

steps.title: Do they argue about שמואל's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about שמואל's rule: if a master gives up ownership of his slave, the slave goes free and needs no גט שחרור.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue about שמואל's rule? שמואל said: one who gives up ownership of his slave, the slave goes free and does not need a document of freedom.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to explain the מחלוקת in the משנה by linking it to a rule of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that once a master gives up ownership, the slave is free even without a גט שחרור. The suggestion is that a slave who ran away is like that, free in practice. So whether he is now bound by his נזירות may depend on whether you accept שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)
A document that sets a slave free

steps.confusionAlert: 'לימא' is only a suggestion. It does not mean the גמרא has decided that this is the reason for the מחלוקת.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shall we say they argue about the rule of Shmuel?
For Shmuel said:
One who gives up ownership of his slave,
the slave goes out to freedom,
and he does not need a document of freedom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to find the reason behind the מחלוקת in the משנה of step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the מחלוקת of רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי depends on שמואל's rule about a slave whose master gave up ownership.

steps.title: Spelling out the suggestion: רבי מאיר holds like שמואל and רבי יוסי does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the suggestion: רבי מאיר holds like שמואל, and רבי יוסי does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: So רבי מאיר holds like שמואל, and רבי יוסי does not hold like שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the suggestion would mean for each תנא. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will examine whether this is really right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the suggestion, רבי מאיר treats the runaway slave as free, so his נזירות applies and he may not drink. רבי יוסי treats him as still a slave, so he may drink. This finishes the לימא suggestion, which the next step rejects.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not hold this view

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds like Shmuel.
Rabbi Yosei does not hold like Shmuel.
phrases.notes: This is still part of the suggestion: if they argue about שמואל, this is how each side would line up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the suggestion of step 14 for each תנא, setting up the next move.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can we really say that רבי מאיר follows שמואל and רבי יוסי rejects him?

steps.title: Everyone agrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about שמואל's rule. Both agree with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'no' to its own suggestion: the two תנאים do not argue about שמואל's rule. It is setting up a different explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 suggested that רבי מאיר follows שמואל and רבי יוסי does not. That suggestion is now dropped, because both can accept שמואל's rule. So the reason for their argument must be something else.

keyTerms.meaning: No. Used here to reject the suggestion just made.
Literally 'the whole world'. It means everyone, here both רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: No, everyone
holds like Shmuel.
phrases.notes: This is שמואל's rule from Step 14: if a master gives up ownership of his slave, the slave goes free.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion from Steps 14 and 15 that the dispute depends on שמואל's rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי disagree about שמואל's rule.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both תנאים can accept שמואל's rule, so their argument does not depend on it.

steps.title: The real reason they argue: will the slave come back?
steps.stepSummary: Both views assume the slave is still owned, because his master never gave him up. רבי יוסי says he will come back in the end anyway, so let him drink and stay strong. רבי מאיר forbids wine so that the hardship pushes him to come home.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the one who says he may drink holds that in the end he will come back to his master, so let him drink wine so he does not grow weak. The one who says he may not drink holds that he should suffer, so that he will come back to his master.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new explanation for the argument between רבי יוסי and רבי מאיר. They agree on the law of ownership and differ about what is better for the master.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions look at the master's interest. רבי יוסי says the slave will come back anyway, so he should drink wine and stay strong enough to work. רבי מאיר says keeping wine from him causes hardship, and that hardship will push him to return.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees with שמואל. The argument about the runaway slave who took נזירות is a practical one: רבי יוסי says let him drink so he stays strong for his master, and רבי מאיר says don't, so the hardship pushes him back home.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up who says what. 'He may drink' is רבי יוסי, and 'he may not drink' is רבי מאיר, the same as in the משנה from Step 13.

phrases.english: Rather: the one who says he may drink holds:
in the end he will surely return
and come back to him (his master),
so let him drink wine
so that he does not grow weak.
And according to the one who says he may not drink, he holds:
let him have suffering
so that he will return to him (his master).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 16 rejected the שמואל explanation, this step gives a new reason for the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of what the dispute is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute depended on whether a master who gives up ownership frees his slave, as in שמואל's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees with שמואל. They argue about whether wine or hardship better serves the master of a slave who will return.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי: the slave drinks so he stays strong. רבי מאיר: he does not drink, so the hardship pushes him to return.
